scope: Unadopted moving-lid extension correctness and evidence honesty; full-head craft remains unmet

primaryBrowser.attribution: Executed by primary, not independently rerun
primaryBrowser.qualification: Three selected people, front/three-quarter/profile, closed color/clay. Eye-globe-removal test compares actual RGB pixels and proves coverage for these cases, not all possible anatomy or GPUs.

sourceObservations: GPU moves separate material-encoded lid strips, while the eye feature aperture remains constant; CPU position oracle agrees with encoded GPU deformation in the focused test
Upper/lower margins meet at blink1; outer v1 folds remain invariant through blink; finite blink is clamped and nonfinite pose refused
Open/close camera draws do not rewrite saved meshes or person inputs. Reopen pixel equality asserted in primary browser test
Squared shader expressions use multiplication rather than undefined signed pow bases; no evidence attributes the original corner leak to that separate correction

findings.description: Native closed/clay images show thick bulged folds rather than convincing soft eyelids; mobile closure is readable but mouth, cap/wire hair, painted beard, thin ear and simple neck remain mannequin-like. Full adult-person target is unmet.

Pose-fixed outer folds are not a proof of watertight lid-to-head topology. This remains separate overlapping prototype surfaces, with analytic/estimated shading normals rather than measured eyelid anatomy.

historicalEvidence: Twelve initial incomplete-closure captures are qualified failure evidence; their initial renderer was not frozen. They are not accepted current renders or a source-bound old implementation proof.
limits: No independent WebGL rerun; primary closure evidence verified structurally and hash-bound
No production integration, animation lifecycle/save-career/accessibility/current suite/release acceptance
Artistic coefficients; no population/medical or observed-eyelid calibration
Maximum mesh budget is a tested default full-hair/full-beard case, not a universal extreme-tessellation budget
